{1} This is an explanation of His complete greatness, His unique oneness in every respect, and the abundance of His good and kindness. So He says: {Blessed}; that is, He is exalted, His attributes are perfect, and His bounties are abundant. Among the greatest of His bounties and favours is that He sent down this Qur'an, which distinguishes between the lawful and the unlawful, guidance and misguidance, and the people of happiness from the people of wretchedness, {upon His servant}: Muhammad ﷺ, who perfected the ranks of servitude and surpassed all the messengers. {That he may be}: that sending down of the Criterion (al-Furqan) upon His servant is {a warner to the worlds}: he warns them of God's might and His vengeance, and makes clear to them the things that bring God's pleasure and those that bring His wrath. Whoever accepts his warning and acts upon it will be among the saved in this world and the Hereafter, those who attain eternal happiness and everlasting dominion. Is there anything beyond this blessing, this bounty and this kindness? So blessed is He, of whose kindness and blessings this is [a part].

{2} {To Whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth}; that is, He alone has disposal over them, and all who are in them are His possessions and servants, submissive to His greatness, subject to His lordship, and in need of His mercy. {He has not taken a son, and He has no partner in dominion}: How could He have a son or a partner, when He is the Owner and others are owned, He is the Subduer and others are subdued, He is self-sufficient in every respect and the creatures are in need of Him [with an essential need] in every respect? And how could He have a partner in dominion when the forelocks of all the servants are in His hand, so they do not move or rest and do not act except by His permission? Exalted is God far above that, with supreme exaltation. Whoever said that did not esteem Him with His true esteem. Therefore He says: {And He created everything}: encompassing the upper world and the lower world, its animals, plants and inanimate things, {and assigned it a precise measure}; that is, He gave every creature among them what befits it and suits it of form, and what His wisdom requires of that. So every creature is such that sound reason cannot conceive it to be other than its shape and its observed form; indeed every part and organ of a single creature is not suited to any place other than the one in which it is. It is therefore fitting that He mention the falsehood of worshipping anything other than Him, so He says:

{3} That is: among the most astonishing wonders, and the clearest proof of their foolishness and deficiency of intellect, or rather, a proof of their wrongdoing and audacity toward their Lord, is that they have taken as gods beings with this attribute: in utter powerlessness, they cannot create anything; rather, they themselves are created, and some of them are even things their own hands have made. {And they possess no power to harm or benefit themselves} — that is, not even a little or a lot, since it is an indefinite noun in the context of negation. {And they possess no power over death, nor life, nor resurrection} — that is, raising up after death.

The most fundamental of the judgments of reason is the invalidity of their divinity, its corruption, and the corruption of the intellect of whoever takes them as gods and partners to the Creator of all creatures, without any share with Him in that, the One in whose hand is benefit and harm, giving and withholding, who gives life and causes death, who resurrects those in the graves and gathers them on the Day of Resurrection. He has appointed for them two abodes: the abode of misery, disgrace and punishment for whoever takes other gods along with Him, and the abode of success, happiness and everlasting bliss for whoever takes Him alone as the object of worship.

When He had established, by a decisive and clear proof, the soundness of monotheism and the invalidity of its opposite, He then established the soundness of prophethood and the invalidity of the view of whoever opposes and objects to it, saying:

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 25, verses 4–6:

{4} That is: And the disbelievers in Allah said, whose disbelief caused them to say about the Qur'an and the Messenger: "This Qur'an is nothing but a lie, which Muhammad has fabricated, and a falsehood he has invented against Allah, and other people have assisted him in that." So Allah refuted them: this is obstinacy on their part and a daring transgression into injustice and falsehood that cannot enter the mind of anyone. They are the people most knowledgeable of the condition of the Messenger (ﷺ), his perfect truthfulness, his trustworthiness and his complete righteousness. Neither he nor any of creation could produce this Qur'an, which is the most sublime and exalted speech, and he had not met anyone who could assist him in that. {So they have brought} with this statement {injustice and falsehood}.

{5} Among their other claims about it, they said: what Muhammad has brought is {tales of the ancients which he has had written down}; that is, this is the narratives and legends of the ancients, which mouths relay and everyone transmits, and Muhammad has copied them down. {They are dictated to him morning and evening}. This statement of theirs contains several grave matters:
Among them: their accusing the Messenger, who is the most righteous and truthful of people, of lying and of great audacity.
Among them: their describing this Qur'an, which is the most truthful, greatest and most exalted speech, as a lie and fabrication.
Among them: that implicit in this is their claim that they are able to produce its like, and that a created being, deficient in every respect, could match the perfect Creator, who is perfect in every respect, in one of His attributes, which is speech.
Among them: that the Messenger's condition is well known, and they are the most knowledgeable of people about it, that he could not write and did not meet anyone who would write for him; yet they have claimed that.

{6} Therefore Allah refuted them with His saying: {Say: It was sent down by the One who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth}; that is, it was sent down by the One whose knowledge encompasses everything in the heavens and the earth, the unseen and the witnessed, the openly spoken and the secret; like His saying: {And indeed, it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. The trustworthy Spirit has brought it down upon your heart, that you may be among the warners} (26:192–194). The argument against them is that the One who sent it down is the one whose knowledge encompasses everything. It is impossible and inconceivable that a created being would fabricate this Qur'an and say it is from Allah when it is not from Him, and would make lawful the blood and property of those who oppose him, claiming that Allah said that to him, while Allah knows everything; and moreover, He supports and helps him against his enemies and grants him power over their necks and lands. No one can deny this Qur'an except by denying the knowledge of Allah, and no group of the children of Adam holds this view except the materialist philosophers.
Also: the mention of His all-encompassing knowledge alerts them and urges them to reflect upon the Qur'an, and that if they reflected, they would see in it of His knowledge and rulings what decisively proves that it could only come from the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed.
And despite their denial of Monotheism and prophethood, it is part of Allah's kindness towards them that He did not leave them in their wrongdoing, but called them to repentance and turning back to Him, and promised them forgiveness and mercy if they repent and return. So He said: {Indeed, He is ever Forgiving}; that is, forgiveness is His attribute toward the people of transgressions and sins when they take the means of forgiveness, which is abandoning His disobedience and repenting from it. {Merciful}: toward them, in that He did not hasten punishment against them though they had committed what requires it, and in that He accepts their repentance after sins, and in that He erases what preceded of their misdeeds, and in that He accepts their good deeds, and in that He restores the one who returns to Him after straying and the one who turns to Him after turning away to the state of the obedient who turn to Him in repentance.

{7} This is from the speech of those who denied the Messenger, by which they cast doubt upon his mission. They objected that it would have been better if he were an angel, or a king, or if an angel accompanied him to assist him. So they said: {What is wrong with this Messenger?}; that is: what is wrong with this one who claims to be a messenger, mocking and deriding him, {that he eats food}: and this is among the characteristics of humans; so why was he not an angel who does not eat food and does not need what humans need? {And walks about in the markets}: for buying and selling, which in their opinion is not befitting for one who is a messenger; yet God said: {And We did not send before you any messengers except that they ate food and walked about in the markets} (25:20). {Why has an angel not been sent down to him}; that is: why was an angel not sent down with him to support and assist him {so that he might be a warner with him}: and in their view he is not sufficient for the mission, nor is he capable by his own strength of carrying it out.

{8} {Or a treasure be thrown down to him}; that is: wealth gathered without effort, {or he have a garden from which he eats}: so that he might be independent of walking in the markets to seek provision. {And the wrongdoers said}: their wrongdoing led them to say it, not confusion on their part: {You follow none but a man affected by sorcery}: and yet they knew his perfect intellect, his good speech, and his freedom from all defects.

{9} Since these statements of theirs were extremely strange, God said: {Look how they strike similitudes for you}: namely, [saying] why was he not an angel, free of human characteristics; or an angel accompanied him, since he is unable to do what he claims; or a treasure was sent down to him; or a garden was made for him that would make him independent of walking in the markets; or that he is affected by sorcery. {So they have gone astray and cannot find a way}: they uttered contradictory statements, all of them ignorance, misguidance and foolishness, none of which contains guidance. Rather, none of them contains even the slightest doubt that could cast doubt upon the mission; merely by looking at them and conceiving them, the intelligent person is certain of their falsehood, and this suffices him in refuting them. For this reason God commanded looking at them, reflecting upon them, and considering whether they necessitate suspending firm belief in the Messenger and his truthfulness.

{10} For this reason He informed that He is able to give you much good in this world, so He said: {Blessed is He who, if He wills, will give you better than that}; that is: better than what they said. Then He explained it with His saying: {gardens beneath which rivers flow, and He will make for you palaces}: lofty and ornamented. His power and will do not fall short of that; but since the world is in His sight of utmost remoteness and insignificance, He gave from it to His friends and messengers what His wisdom required. The demand of their enemies that they should have been given very abundant provision from it is injustice and audacity.

{11} Since those statements they uttered were known to be corrupt, God informed that they did not proceed from them in seeking the truth nor in following proof, but proceeded from them out of obstinacy, wrongdoing and denial of the truth; they said what was in their hearts. For this reason He said: {Nay, they deny the Hour}: the denier who is obstinate and has no intention of following the truth has no path to his guidance and no means of arguing with him; he has only one means, which is the descent of punishment upon him. Therefore He said: {And We have prepared for those who deny the Hour a blazing Fire}; that is: a great fire whose blaze has intensified, which is enraged against its people, and whose roar has become severe.

{12} {When it sees them from a distant place}; that is: before they reach it and it reaches them; {they hear its raging}: against them {and roaring}: by which hearts are terrified, hearts are split, and one of them almost dies from fear and terror. It has become angry at them with the anger of its Creator, and its flame has increased because of the increase of their disbelief and evil.

{13} {And when they are thrown into a narrow place therein, chained together}; that is: at the time of their punishment, while they are gathered together in its midst, combining the narrowness of the place, the crowding of its inhabitants, and their being bound together with chains and shackles. When they arrive at that ill-omened place and are imprisoned in the worst of prisons, {they will call out there for destruction}: they call upon themselves for destruction, disgrace and shame, knowing that they were wrongdoers and transgressors, and that the Creator has justly dealt with them in placing them in this abode because of their deeds.

{14} That supplication and pleading will not benefit them nor save them from the punishment of God. Rather it will be said to them: {Do not call out today for one destruction, but call out for many destructions}; that is: even if what you say were multiplied many times over, it would benefit you only with distress, grief and sorrow.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 25, verse 15–16:

{15} That is, say to them, showing the foolishness of their opinion and their choice of what harms over what benefits: {Is that better, or the Garden of Eternity which the God-fearing have been promised?} The Garden whose provision is piety toward God. Whoever establishes piety, God has promised it to him. {It shall be a reward for them} for their piety, {and a destination} (maseer), a refuge to which they return, in which they settle, and in which they abide forever, eternally.

{16} {For them therein is whatever they wish}; that is, whatever they seek and whatever their hopes and desires attach to: of foods, delicious drinks, splendid garments, beautiful women, lofty palaces, gardens and orchards of dense foliage (1), and fruits that delight the eyes of those who look at them and those who eat them, by their beauty, variety and abundance of kinds; and rivers flowing through the meadows and orchards of the Garden, which they direct and cause to gush wherever they wish: rivers of water that has not turned putrid, rivers of milk whose taste has not changed, rivers of wine, a delight to those who drink, and rivers of purified honey, and fragrant scents, and elegant dwellings, and melodious voices that captivate hearts by their beauty, and visiting one's brothers, and enjoying meeting the beloved. Higher than all of this is the enjoyment of looking upon the face of the Merciful Lord, hearing His speech, enjoying closeness to Him, the happiness of His good pleasure, and safety from His wrath, and the continuance of this bliss, its permanence, and its increase as time passes and moments follow one another. {It is, upon your Lord, a promise to be asked for} (masool): His servants who are God-fearing ask Him for it, by the tongue of their state and the tongue of their speech.

So which of the two abodes mentioned is better and more worthy of preference? And which of the two groups of workers, the workers of the abode of wretchedness or the workers of the abode of happiness, is more worthy of virtue, intellect and pride, O people of understanding? The truth has become clear and the path has been illuminated, so the negligent person has no excuse for abandoning the proof. We hope from You, O One who has decreed wretchedness for some peoples and happiness for others, that You make us among those for whom You have written the best and more. We seek refuge in You, O Allah, from the state of the wretched, and we ask You for well-being from it.

At that time they will seek refuge from the angels and flee, but there is no escape for them. ﴿And they will say, "A forbidding, forbidden [barrier]."﴾ ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass through; you will not pass except with authority.﴾

{23} ﴿And We will advance toward what they did of deeds﴾: that is, their deeds which they hoped would be good and in which they labored. ﴿And We will make them scattered dust﴾: that is, void and dissolved; they have lost them, were deprived of their reward, and were punished for them. This is due to their lacking faith and their being issued from one who denies Allah and His messengers. The deed that Allah accepts is only that which proceeds from the sincere believer who affirms the messengers and follows them in it.

On that terrible day, full of turmoil, {the companions of Paradise} — those who believed in God, did righteous deeds and feared their Lord — {will be better in their dwelling place} than the people of the Fire, {and finer in their resting place}. That is, their dwelling place in Paradise and their rest, which is the midday repose (al-qaylulah), is a beneficial dwelling and complete comfort, because this includes perfect bliss, unmixed with any turbidity. This is unlike the companions of the Fire, for Hell is their dwelling place, and it is evil as a dwelling place and as a resting place. This is an instance of using the comparative form (af'al al-tafdil, the elative) where the other side has nothing of the quality at all, since there is no good at all in the resting place or dwelling place of the people of the Fire, like His saying: ﴿Is God better, or what they associate with Him?﴾

{25–26} He, exalted is He, informs about the greatness of the Day of Resurrection and what it contains of severity, distress, and heart-shaking terrors. He says: ﴿And the Day when the heaven will be split open with clouds﴾. That cloud is the one in which Allah descends; it comes down from above the heavens, and the heavens are cleft and split open for it, and the angels of each heaven descend. They stand in rows: either one row encompassing the creation, or each heaven has its own row, then the heaven that follows it has a row, and so on. The point is that the angels, despite their multitude and might, descend encompassing creation, submissive to the command of their Lord, and none of them speaks except by Allah's permission. So what do you suppose about the weak human being, especially one who defied his Master with great sins and rushed into what angers Him, and then came before Him with sins and transgressions he never repented of? The Sovereign, the Creator, will judge him with a judgment that does not wrong, not even to the weight of an atom. Hence He says: ﴿and it will be a difficult day for the disbelievers﴾, because of its extreme hardship and the difficulty of its affairs for them, unlike the believer, for whom it is easy and its burden light. ﴿And the Day We will gather the God-fearing to the Most Merciful as a delegation, and drive the criminals to Hell as a thirsty herd.﴾ And His saying ﴿The dominion that Day belongs to the Most Merciful﴾: that is, the Day of Resurrection. ﴿The sovereignty, that Day, belongs to the Most Merciful﴾: no dominion, nor even the semblance of dominion, remains for any created being, as they had in this world; rather, kings and their subjects, free and slave, nobles and others, will all be equal.

Among what delights the heart, calms the soul, and expands the breast is that He attributed sovereignty on the Day of Resurrection to His name the Most Merciful, whose mercy encompasses everything, embraces every living thing, fills all beings, and by which this world and the Hereafter are made prosperous; by it every deficiency is completed and every lack removed. The names indicating mercy have overcome the names indicating wrath, and His mercy has preceded and overcome His anger; to it belong precedence and dominance. He created this weak human being, honored and ennobled him, so that He might complete His blessing upon him and envelop him with His mercy. They will be present in a station of humility, submission, and abasement before Him, awaiting what He will decide concerning them and what He will carry out upon them, and He is more merciful to them than they are to themselves and their parents. So consider how He will deal with them. None perishes before Allah except one who is destined to perish, and none is excluded from His mercy except one over whom wretchedness has prevailed and upon whom the word of punishment has been fulfilled.

{27} ﴿And the Day the wrongdoer will bite his hands﴾: because of his polytheism, disbelief, and denial of the messengers, ﴿saying: "Would that I had taken a way with the Messenger!"﴾; that is, a path of faith in him, believing in him and following him.

{28} ﴿Woe to me! Would that I had not taken such-and-such a person﴾: that is, the human or jinn devil ﴿as a close friend﴾; that is, a sincere beloved. I opposed the one who advised me most, was most kind to me, and was most gentle with me, and I befriended the greatest enemy to me, whose friendship brought me nothing but misery, loss, disgrace, and ruin.

{29} ﴿He led me astray from the Reminder after it had come to me﴾: since he made appear to him the misguidance he was upon through his deceit and enticement, ﴿and Satan is ever a betrayer of man﴾: he adorns falsehood for him, makes truth ugly to him, promises him false hopes, and then abandons him and disowns him, as he said to all his followers when the matter was decided and Allah had finished the reckoning of creation: ﴿And Satan will say when the matter has been decided: "Indeed, Allah promised you a true promise, and I promised you, but I failed you. I had no authority over you except that I called you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me; blame yourselves. I cannot help you, nor can you help me. Indeed, I disbelieve in your associating me with Allah before..."﴾ — the verse. So let the servant look to his own soul while there is still opportunity, let him seize what is possible before it becomes impossible, and let him befriend the one whose friendship brings him happiness, and oppose the one whose enmity benefits him and whose friendship harms him. And Allah is the Granter of success.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 25, verses 30–31:

{30} {And the Messenger said}: calling out to his Lord and complaining to Him about the aversion of his people to what he had brought, and expressing grief over this from them: {O my Lord, indeed my people have taken this Qur'an as something abandoned}, meaning: those whom You sent me to guide and to convey to. That is, they have turned away from it, shunned it and left it, even though it was obligatory for them to submit to its judgment, to turn toward its rulings, and to follow it.

{31} Allah said, consoling His Messenger and informing him: indeed these creatures have predecessors who did as they did. So He said: {And thus We have appointed for every prophet an enemy from among the criminals}, meaning: from among those who are not fit for goodness and do not purify themselves by it; they oppose them, refute them, and dispute with them using falsehood. Among the benefits of this is that the truth may prevail over falsehood, that the truth may become clear and be manifested in a great manifestation; for the opposition of falsehood to truth is something that increases it in clarity, explanation, and perfection of proof. And that we may see what Allah does to the people of truth in terms of honor, and to the people of falsehood in terms of punishment. So do not grieve over them, and do not let your soul waste away in regret over them. {And your Lord suffices as a guide}: He guides you, so that you attain what you seek and the welfare of your religion and your worldly life. {And as a helper}: He helps you against your enemies and repels from you every harm in matters of religion and the world. So be content with Him and put your trust in Him.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 25, verse 32–33:

{32} This is among the suggestions of the disbelievers, which their own souls inspired in them. They said: ﴿Why was the Qur'an not sent down to him all at once?﴾ That is, just as the (previous) Books were sent down before him. And what objection is there to its being sent down in this manner? Rather, sending it down in this manner is more perfect and better. For this reason He said: ﴿Thus﴾ (We sent it down gradually), ﴿so that We may strengthen your heart thereby﴾ — because every time a portion of the Qur'an descended upon him, he grew in tranquility and steadfastness, especially when causes of anxiety arose. The descent of the Qur'an at the moment an event occurs has a great effect and much greater reinforcement than if it had descended beforehand and he then recalled it when its cause came about. ﴿And We have arranged it in gradual arrangement﴾; that is, We made it spread out, and We brought you up through it by degrees.

All of this indicates Allah's care for His Book, the Qur'an, and for His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), in that He made the sending down of His Book follow the circumstances of the Messenger and his religious interests.

{33} For this reason He said: ﴿And they do not bring you any example except that We bring you the truth and better explanation﴾; that is, they use it to oppose the truth and to repel your message. ﴿Except that We bring you the truth and better explanation﴾; that is, We sent down to you a Qur'an that comprises the truth in its meanings, and clarity and complete exposition in its wording. Its meanings are all truth and veracity, with no falsehood or doubt mixed into them in any way, and its words and definitions of things are the clearest in expression and the best in explanation, clarifying the meanings with complete clarity.

In this verse is evidence that whoever speaks on knowledge, whether a narrator of hadith, a teacher, or a preacher, should follow his Lord in His management of the affairs of His Messenger. Likewise, the scholar manages the affairs of creation, and whenever a cause arises or an occasion occurs, he brings what suits that from the Qur'anic verses, the Prophetic hadiths, and the admonitions that accord with it.

In it is also a refutation of the over-elaborate Jahmiyyah and others like them, who hold that many texts of the Qur'an are to be understood other than their apparent meaning, and that they have meanings other than what is understood from them. According to their view, then, the Qur'an would not be the better explanation compared with anything else; rather, the better explanation in their claim is their own explanation, by which they distorted the meanings into distortion!

{33} For this reason He said: ﴿And they do not bring you any example except that We bring you the truth and better explanation﴾; that is, they use it to oppose the truth and to repel your message. ﴿Except that We bring you the truth and better explanation﴾; that is, We sent down to you a Qur'an that comprises the truth in its meanings, and clarity and complete exposition in its wording. Its meanings are all truth and veracity, with no falsehood or doubt mixed into them in any way, and its words and definitions of things are the clearest in expression and the best in explanation, clarifying the meanings with complete clarity.

In this verse is evidence that whoever speaks on knowledge, whether a narrator of hadith, a teacher, or a preacher, should follow his Lord in His management of the affairs of His Messenger. Likewise, the scholar manages the affairs of creation, and whenever a cause arises or an occasion occurs, he brings what suits that from the Qur'anic verses, the Prophetic hadiths, and the admonitions that accord with it.

In it is also a refutation of the over-elaborate Jahmiyyah and others like them, who hold that many texts of the Qur'an are to be understood other than their apparent meaning, and that they have meanings other than what is understood from them. According to their view, then, the Qur'an would not be the better explanation compared with anything else; rather, the better explanation in their claim is their own explanation, by which they distorted the meanings into distortion!

{34} He, may He be exalted, informs of the state of the polytheists who denied His Messenger and of their evil end: that they "will be gathered on their faces" in the most hideous sight and the most horrific appearance, the angels of punishment dragging them and pulling them "to Hell" (Jahannam), which encompasses every kind of torment and retribution. "Those" who are in this condition are "worse in place" than those who believed in Allah and affirmed His messengers, and "further astray in way." This is from the usage of the comparative form (af'al al-tafdil) in a case where the other party has no share in the matter at all; for the believers have a good place and a good abode, and they were guided in this world to the Straight Path, and in the Hereafter they reach the Gardens of Bliss.

Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 25, verses 35–40:

{35–40} God, exalted is He, alluded to these stories, although He had elaborated them in other verses, in order to warn those being addressed against persisting in denying their Messenger, lest there befall them what befell those nations who were close to them, and whose stories they know through what has been widely transmitted and become well known about them. Some of them see their traces with their own eyes, such as the people of Salih in al-Hijr, and the town that was rained upon with the rain of evil, with stones of sijjil; you pass by them in the morning and at night in your journeys. Those nations were no worse than these, and their messengers were no better than the messenger of these people. ﴿Are your disbelievers better than those, or do you have immunity in the Scriptures?﴾ But what prevented these people from believing, despite what they witnessed of the signs, is that they did not hope for resurrection or rising again; so they did not hope to meet their Lord, nor did they fear His punishment. Therefore they persisted in their obstinacy. Otherwise, there had come to them signs that leave no room for doubt, dubiety, confusion, or uncertainty.

{41} That is, when ﴿they see you﴾, O Muhammad, these deniers of you, who obstinately oppose the signs of God and act arrogantly on earth, mock you and belittle you. They say, in a manner of contempt and disparagement: ﴿Is this the one whom God has sent as a messenger?﴾ That is, it is improper and unfitting that God should send this man! This is from the extent of their wrongdoing, obstinacy, and their inversion of realities. Their words imply that the Messenger, far be it from him, is of the utmost baseness and insignificance, and that if messengerhood had been given to someone else, it would have been more fitting. They also say: ﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a great man from the two cities?﴾ Such speech comes only from the most ignorant and misguided of people, or from the greatest of the obstinate, who feigns ignorance, whose aim is to promote the falsehood they hold by disparaging the truth and the one who brought it. Otherwise, whoever reflects on the circumstances of Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah (peace be upon him) will find him to be the most learned of men, their leader and foremost in intellect, knowledge, sound judgment, gravity, noble character, excellent disposition, chastity, courage, generosity, and every virtuous trait. Meanwhile, the one who belittles him and hates him has combined foolishness, ignorance, error, contradiction, injustice, and transgression in a way no one else combines them. It is enough of a sign of his ignorance and misguidance that he disparages this great Messenger and noble man. The purpose of their disparagement of him and their mockery of him is to remain firm in their falsehood and to deceive weak-minded people.

{42} For this reason they said: ﴿He almost led us astray from our gods﴾ [this man], by making the gods into one God. ﴿Had we not been steadfast in worshipping them﴾, he would have led us astray. They claimed, may God curse them, that error is monotheism (tawhid, the affirmation of God's oneness), and that guidance is what they held of polytheism (shirk, associating partners with God). Ibn Sa'di's commentary on Surah 25, verses 45–46:

{45–46} That is: Have you not considered, with your sight and your insight, the perfection of your Lord's power and the vastness of His mercy? He extended the shade over the servants, and that was before the rising of the sun. ﴿Then We made the sun its evidence﴾; that is, the sun is the evidence of the shade. Were it not for the existence of the sun, the shade would not be recognized, for opposites are known by their opposites. ﴿Then We withdraw it to Us, a gradual withdrawal﴾. So whenever the sun rises, the shade contracts little by little until it disappears completely. Thus the succession of shade and sun over creation, which they witness with their own eyes, and what follows from it of the alternation of night and day, the succession of the seasons, and the many benefits that result from this, is among the clearest proofs of God's power and greatness, of His perfect mercy and care for His servants, and that He alone is the one worthy of worship, the praised, the beloved, the exalted, Lord of majesty and honour.

{47} That is: out of His mercy toward you and His kindness, He made the night for you like a garment that covers you, so that you may settle in it and be at rest through sleep, and your movements may cease; that is, they are cut off at sleep. Had it not been for the night, the servants would not have been still, nor would they have continued in their affairs, and that would have harmed them in the extreme. And had the darkness also continued, their livelihoods and their interests would have been brought to a standstill. But He made the day a nushur (a time of dispersal), in which they spread out for their trade, their travels and their work, and by this the various interests are upheld.

{48–49} That is, He alone is the One who showed mercy to His servants and bestowed His provision upon them by sending the winds as bearers of good news before His mercy, which is the rain. The winds stir up the clouds and gather them together, so that they become fragments, and they fertilize them and cause them to pour forth, by the leave of the One who commands them and directs them. This is so that the servants may rejoice in the rain before it falls, and prepare for it before it comes upon them all at once. ﴿And We send down from the sky pure water﴾: it purifies from minor and major ritual impurity (hadath and khabath), and it purifies from impurities and filth. Among its blessings is that He sent it down to give life to a dead land, so that various kinds of vegetation and trees grow in it, of which men and cattle eat. ﴿That We may give drink to many of the cattle and people that We have created﴾; that is, We give you and your cattle to drink. Is not He who sent the winds as bearers of good news, who made them diverse in their work, and who sent down from the sky pure, blessed water, in which is the provision of the servants and the provision of their beasts, the One who deserves to be worshipped alone, and not to have anything associated with Him?

{50} When the Exalted mentioned these visible, observed signs, and directed them to the servants so that they would know Him, thank Him, and remember Him, yet despite this, ﴿most of the people refuse except disbelief﴾, due to the corruption of their characters and natures.

The winds stir up the clouds and gather them together, so that they become fragments, and they fertilize them and cause them to pour forth, by the leave of the One who commands them and directs them. This is so that the servants may rejoice in the rain before it falls, and prepare for it before it comes upon them all at once. ﴿And We send down from the sky pure water﴾: it purifies from minor and major ritual impurity (hadath and khabath), and it purifies from impurities and filth. Among its blessings is that He sent it down to give life to a dead land, so that various kinds of vegetation and trees grow in it, of which men and cattle eat. ﴿That We may give drink to many of the cattle and people that We have created﴾; that is, We give you and your cattle to drink. Is not He who sent the winds as bearers of good news, who made them diverse in their work, and who sent down from the sky pure, blessed water, in which is the provision of the servants and the provision of their beasts, the One who deserves to be worshipped alone, and not to have anything associated with Him?

{50} When the Exalted mentioned these visible, observed signs, and directed them to the servants so that they would know Him, thank Him, and remember Him, yet despite this, ﴿most of the people refuse except disbelief﴾, due to the corruption of their characters and natures.

{51} He, may He be exalted, informs of the execution of His will, and that if He willed, He would have sent a warner (nadhir) to every town; that is, a messenger who warns and admonishes them. His will is not deficient in doing so, but His wisdom and His mercy toward you and toward the servants, O Muhammad, required that He send you to all of them: their red and their black, their Arab and their non-Arab, their humans and their jinn.

{52} {So do not obey the disbelievers}: in abandoning anything of what you were sent with. Rather, exert your utmost effort in conveying what you were sent with. {And strive against them}: with the Qur'an, {a great striving}; that is, do not leave any of your effort in supporting the truth and suppressing falsehood unexpended, even if you see from them such denial and audacity as you see. So exert your effort, expend your full capacity, do not despair of their guidance, and do not leave off conveying to them because of their desires.

{53} That is: {And He it is} alone {Who released the two seas} so that they meet: the sweet sea, which are the rivers flowing over the face of the earth, and the salty sea. He made the benefit of each one of them a good for the servants. {And He placed between them a barrier}, that is, a partition that prevents one of them from mixing with the other, so that the intended benefit of each would be lost; {and a forbidding partition}, that is, a strong, impregnable barrier.

{54} That is: He is God alone, with no partner, who created the human being from a base fluid (ma'in mahin), then spread from it numerous offspring, and made them into lineages (ansab) and marriage relations (aṣhar), scattered and gathered, while the whole substance is from that base water. This indicates the perfection of His power, by His saying: ﴿And your Lord is ever Competent﴾, and it indicates that His worship is the truth and the worship of other than Him is false, by His saying:

{55} That is: they worship idols and dead things that neither harm nor benefit, and they set them up as rivals to the Owner of benefit and harm, of giving and withholding. Yet it was obligatory upon them to be guided by the directions of their Lord, defending His religion, but they reversed the matter. {And the disbelIever is ever a helper against his Lord} ﴿وكان الكافر على ربه ظهيرا﴾: falsehood, which is the idols and rivals, are enemies of God; so the disbeliever assists them and backs them against their Lord, and becomes an enemy of his Lord, waging open enmity and war against Him. This, though He is the One who created him, provided for him, and bestowed upon him outward and inward blessings, and he is not outside His dominion, authority, and control; and God has not withheld from him His kindness and goodness, yet he, in his ignorance, continues in this hostility and open opposition.

{56} Allah, the Exalted, informs us that He did not send His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) to exercise control over the creation, nor did He make him an angel, nor did he have the treasuries of all things. Rather, He sent him as ﴿a bringer of good tidings﴾: he gives good tidings to those who obey Allah of reward, both in this world swiftly and in the Hereafter. And ﴿a warner﴾: he warns those who disobey Allah of punishment, both in this world swiftly and in the Hereafter. This necessarily entails clarifying what the good tidings consist of, and what the warning consists of, namely the commands and prohibitions.

{57} And you, O Muhammad, do not ask them for any wage for conveying the Qur'an and guidance, lest that prevent them from following you, and they burden themselves with expense. ﴿Except for whoever wills to take a way to his Lord﴾: that is, except for whoever wills to spend some expenditure in seeking the pleasure of his Lord and in His way. This, although I encourage you to it, I do not compel you to it, and it is also not a wage for me from you. Rather, it returns to your own benefit and to your following of the path that leads to your Lord.

{58} Then He commanded him to rely upon Him and to seek His help, saying: ﴿And rely upon the Living﴾, the One who possesses complete and absolute life, ﴿who does not die. And glorify Him with His praise﴾: that is, worship Him and rely upon Him in matters concerning you and concerning the creation. ﴿And sufficient is He as one who is Acquainted with the sins of His servants﴾: He knows them and will recompense for them. So you, there is nothing upon you concerning their guidance, nor upon you is the preservation of their deeds; all of that is in the hand of Allah.

{59} ﴿He who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days; then He established Himself﴾ thereafter ﴿upon the Throne﴾, which is the ceiling of the creatures, the highest, the widest, and the most beautiful of them. ﴿The Most Merciful﴾: He established Himself upon His Throne, which encompasses the heavens and the earth, by His name the Most Merciful, whose mercy encompasses all things. Thus He established Himself upon the widest of creatures with the widest of attributes. By this verse He affirmed His creating of creatures, His knowledge of their outward and inward states, His being high above the Throne, and His distinctness from them. ﴿So ask about Him one Acquainted﴾: meaning, about His noble Self. He is the One who knows His attributes, His greatness, and His majesty, and He has informed you of that, and has made clear to you from His greatness that [by which you are made happy] through knowing Him. Those who know Him have known Him and submitted to His majesty, while the disbelievers have been arrogant toward worshipping Him and have disdained that.

{60} For this reason He said: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Prostrate to the Most Merciful,"﴾ that is, to Him alone, who has bestowed upon you all kinds of blessings and warded off from you all afflictions, ﴿they say, "And what is the Most Merciful?"﴾ denying and disbelieving. By their corrupt assumption they claim that they do not know the Most Merciful. And among the things they used as criticisms of the Messenger was that they said: "He forbids us from taking deities alongside Allah, yet he calls upon another god along with Him; he says, 'O Most Merciful!'" and similar things. As Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say, "Call upon Allah or call upon the Most Merciful; whichever you call, to Him belong the most beautiful names."﴾ His names, Exalted is He, are many, due to the multiplicity of His attributes and the diversity of His perfection; each one of them indicates an attribute of perfection. ﴿Shall we prostrate to what you command us?﴾ that is, merely because you command us. This is based on their denial of the Messenger and their arrogance toward obeying him. ﴿And it increased them﴾, the call to prostrate to the Most Merciful, ﴿in aversion﴾: fleeing from the truth to falsehood, and an increase in disbelief and wretchedness.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 25, verses 61–62:

{61} He said: ﴿Blessed is He who placed constellations in the sky﴾. These are the stars in general, or the stations of the sun and the moon, which it traverses station by station. They are like the constellations and the fortresses of cities in protecting them. Likewise, the stars are like the constellations placed for guarding, for they are missiles against the devils. ﴿And He placed therein a lamp﴾, which contains light and heat, and this is the sun. ﴿And a moon giving light﴾, which contains light but not heat. This is among the proofs of His greatness and the abundance of His beneficence, for what is in them of wondrous creation, orderly management, and great beauty indicates the greatness of their Creator in all His attributes. And what is in them of benefits and advantages for creation is evidence of the abundance of His goodness.

{62} ﴿And He it is who made the night and the day succeeding one another﴾, meaning: one of them goes and the other follows it, always in this way, never joining together or ceasing. ﴿For whoever desires to remember or desires to give thanks﴾, meaning: for whoever wishes to remember through them, to take heed, and to be guided by them to many of the divine aims, and to thank God for that; and for whoever wishes to mention God and thank Him. Every servant has a portion of worship in the night or the day, so whoever misses his portion in one of them makes it up in the other. Also, hearts turn and change within the hours of night and day: energy and laziness, remembrance and heedlessness, contraction and expansion, turning toward God and turning away from Him all occur in them. So God made the night and the day follow each other upon the servants and recur, so that remembrance, energy, and thankfulness to God may arise in them at another time. And because the times of worship recur with the recurrence of night and day, whenever the times recur, He produces in the servant a resolve different from the resolve that had grown lax in the earlier time, and so his remembrance and thankfulness increase. Thus the duties of acts of obedience are like the watering of faith that sustains it; were it not for that, the plant of faith would wither and dry up. So to God belongs the most complete and perfect praise for this.

Then he mentioned, among the many aspects of His goodness, His favour upon His righteous servants and His guidance of them to righteous deeds which earned them lofty dwellings in the chambers of Paradise. He said:

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 25, verses 61–62:

{61} He said: ﴿Blessed is He who placed constellations in the sky﴾. These are the stars in general, or the stations of the sun and the moon, which it traverses station by station. They are like the constellations and the fortresses of cities in protecting them. Likewise, the stars are like the constellations placed for guarding, for they are missiles against the devils. ﴿And He placed therein a lamp﴾, which contains light and heat, and this is the sun. ﴿And a moon giving light﴾, which contains light but not heat. This is among the proofs of His greatness and the abundance of His beneficence, for what is in them of wondrous creation, orderly management, and great beauty indicates the greatness of their Creator in all His attributes. And what is in them of benefits and advantages for creation is evidence of the abundance of His goodness.

{62} ﴿And He it is who made the night and the day succeeding one another﴾, meaning: one of them goes and the other follows it, always in this way, never joining together or ceasing. ﴿For whoever desires to remember or desires to give thanks﴾, meaning: for whoever wishes to remember through them, to take heed, and to be guided by them to many of the divine aims, and to thank God for that; and for whoever wishes to mention God and thank Him. Every servant has a portion of worship in the night or the day, so whoever misses his portion in one of them makes it up in the other. Also, hearts turn and change within the hours of night and day: energy and laziness, remembrance and heedlessness, contraction and expansion, turning toward God and turning away from Him all occur in them. So God made the night and the day follow each other upon the servants and recur, so that remembrance, energy, and thankfulness to God may arise in them at another time. And because the times of worship recur with the recurrence of night and day, whenever the times recur, He produces in the servant a resolve different from the resolve that had grown lax in the earlier time, and so his remembrance and thankfulness increase. Thus the duties of acts of obedience are like the watering of faith that sustains it; were it not for that, the plant of faith would wither and dry up. So to God belongs the most complete and perfect praise for this.

Then he mentioned, among the many aspects of His goodness, His favour upon His righteous servants and His guidance of them to righteous deeds which earned them lofty dwellings in the chambers of Paradise. He said:

**Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 25, verses 63–77:**

{63} Servitude to Allah (ʿubudiyyah) is of two kinds. The first is servitude to His lordship (rububiyyah). All of creation shares in this, whether believer or disbeliever, righteous or wicked, for they are all servants of Allah, nurtured and governed by Him. ﴿There is none in the heavens and the earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant﴾.

The second is servitude to His divinity (uluhiyyah), His worship, and His mercy. This is the servitude of His prophets and His friends (awliya'), and it is what is meant here. For this reason He attributed it to His name "the Most Merciful," to indicate that they reached this state only through His mercy. He then mentioned that their attributes are the most perfect attributes and their qualities the most excellent. He described them as ﴿those who walk upon the earth in humility﴾, meaning: calm and humble before Allah and before creation. This is a description of them as possessing gravity, tranquility, and humility before Allah and His servants. ﴿And when the ignorant address them﴾, meaning with the speech of ignorance, as indicated by the attribution of the verb to this description, ﴿they say, "Peace."﴾ That is, they address them with words by which they are safe from sin and safe from responding to ignorance with ignorance. This is praise of them for great forbearance, for repaying evil with good, for pardoning the ignorant, and for the soundness of intellect that brought them to this state.

{64} ﴿And those who spend the night before their Lord, prostrating and standing﴾, meaning: they devote themselves much to the night prayer, sincere in it toward their Lord and humbled before Him, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds, calling upon their Lord in fear and hope, and from what We have provided them they spend. No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes, as reward for what they used to do﴾.

{65} ﴿And those who say, "Our Lord, avert from us the punishment of Hell﴾, meaning: repel it from us by protecting us from its causes and forgiving what has occurred from us that would warrant punishment. ﴿Indeed, its punishment is ever adhering﴾, meaning: it clings to its people as a creditor clings to his debtor.

{66} ﴿Indeed, it is evil as a place of settlement and residence.﴾ This is said by them in humble supplication to their Lord, and to show their great need for Him, and that they have no capacity to bear this punishment. They also remember Allah's favor upon them, for the removal of a hardship is greater in its effect the more severe and dreadful the hardship, and joy in its removal is greater.

{67} ﴿And those who, when they spend﴾, meaning obligatory and recommended expenditures, ﴿neither waste nor are stingy﴾. Waste means exceeding the limit and falling into the category of extravagance. Stinginess means falling into miserliness and avarice, and neglecting obligatory rights. ﴿And their spending is between that﴾, meaning between extravagance and niggardliness, ﴿a means.﴾ They give in obligatory matters, such as zakat, expiations, and obligatory maintenance, and in what is fitting, in the proper manner, without harm or injury. This is from their justice and moderation.

{68} ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity﴾, but worship Him alone, sincere to Him in religion, upright, turning toward Him and turning away from all else. ﴿And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden﴾, meaning the soul of a Muslim and of a disbeliever under covenant, ﴿except by right﴾, such as killing a soul in retaliation, or killing a married adulterer, or a disbeliever whose killing is lawful. ﴿And do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse﴾, but rather guard their private parts, ﴿except with their spouses or what their right hands possess.﴾ ﴿And whoever does that﴾, meaning associating partners with Allah, or killing a soul which Allah has forbidden without right, or fornication, ﴿will meet a penalty.﴾

{69} Then He explained it by His saying: ﴿The punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein humiliated﴾, meaning in the punishment. The threat of eternal abiding applies without doubt to whoever commits all of these, and likewise to whoever associates partners with Allah. Likewise, the threat of severe punishment applies to each of these three, because each is either shirk or among the greatest major sins. As for the eternal abiding of the murderer and the fornicator in punishment, it does not apply to them, because the Qur'anic texts and the prophetic Sunnah have established that all believers will eventually leave the Fire, and no believer will abide in it, no matter what sins he has committed. Allah specified these three because they are the greatest major sins. Shirk entails corruption of religions, killing entails corruption of bodies, and fornication entails corruption of honor.

{70} ﴿Except for one who repents﴾ from these sins and others, by giving them up immediately, regretting what he had done of them in the past, and resolving firmly never to return to them, ﴿and believes﴾ in Allah with sound belief that requires abandoning sins and performing acts of obedience, ﴿and does righteous work﴾ of what the Lawgiver has commanded, when he intends by it the countenance of Allah. ﴿For those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good ones﴾, meaning their actions and words which had been prone to evil deeds will be transformed into good ones. Thus their shirk is transformed into faith, their disobedience into obedience, and the very evil deeds they committed are transformed, after they repent of each sin, turn back in penitence and obedience, into good deeds, as is apparent in the verse. A report concerning this is the hadith of the man whom Allah called to account for some of his sins, enumerating them to him, and then He replaced each evil deed with a good one. He said: "O Lord! I have sins which I do not see here." And Allah knows best. ﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving﴾ to whoever repents, forgiving great sins, ﴿and Merciful﴾ to His servants, for He called them to repentance after they had opposed Him with great sins, then granted them success in it, then accepted it from them.

{71} ﴿And whoever repents and does righteous work — indeed, he turns to Allah with [sincere] return﴾, meaning he should know that his repentance is in the utmost perfection, because it is a return to the path that leads to Allah, which is the very essence of the servant's happiness and success. Therefore let him be sincere in it, and purify it from the impurities of corrupt motives. The purpose of this is to urge the perfecting of repentance and following it in the best and most excellent manner, so that He may advance toward the one who repents to Him and give him his reward according to its perfection.

{72} ﴿And those who do not witness falsehood﴾, meaning they do not attend falsehood, that is, forbidden speech and deeds. Thus they avoid all gatherings that include forbidden speech or forbidden actions, such as delving into the signs of Allah, vain disputation, backbiting, slander, insult, defamation, mockery, forbidden singing, drinking wine, and spreading out silk and images, and the like. If they do not witness falsehood, it is all the more fitting and more certain that they do not utter it or commit it. The bearing of false witness is included under speaking falsehood, and it enters this verse by way of priority. ﴿And when they pass by ill speech﴾, which is speech with no good in it and no religious or worldly benefit, such as the talk of fools and the like, ﴿they pass by with dignity.﴾ That is, they keep themselves pure and honorable, refraining from delving into such things, and they regard delving into them, even if there is no sin in it, as foolishness and a deficiency of humanity and manliness, so they keep themselves far from it. In His saying ﴿when they pass by ill speech﴾ there is an indication that they do not intend to attend it or to listen to it, but if they chance upon it without intention, they keep themselves honorable by avoiding it.

{73} ﴿And those who, when they are reminded of the verses of their Lord﴾, which He commanded them to listen to and to be guided by, ﴿do not fall upon them deaf and blind﴾, meaning they do not meet them with turning away from them, with deafness to hearing them, or with turning their sight and hearts away from them, as those do who do not believe in them or affirm them. Rather their condition regarding them and upon hearing them is as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The only ones who believe in Our verses are those who, when they are reminded of them, fall down in prostration and exalt the praise of their Lord, and they are not arrogant﴾. They meet them with acceptance, with need for them, with submission and surrender to them. You will find with them listening ears and attentive hearts, so their faith increases through them, their certainty is completed through them, they bring them vigor, and they rejoice in them with delight and gladness.

{74} ﴿And those who say, "Our Lord, grant us from among our spouses and offspring comfort for our eyes﴾, meaning our companions, whether friends, peers, or wives, ﴿and offspring who will be a comfort to our eyes﴾, that is, through them our eyes may be comforted. When we consider their condition and attributes, we recognize from their aspirations and the loftiness of their rank that their eyes will not be comforted until they see their spouses and offspring obedient to their Lord, knowing and acting. This supplication for their spouses and offspring for their righteousness is, at the same time, a supplication for themselves, since its benefit returns to them. For this reason they made it a gift to themselves, saying: ﴿Grant us﴾. Moreover, their supplication returns to benefit all Muslims in general, because the righteousness of those mentioned is a cause for the righteousness of many who are connected to them and benefit from them. ﴿And make us a leader for the righteous﴾, that is: bring us, O our Lord, to this high station, the station of the truthful (siddiqin) and the perfected among the righteous servants of Allah, which is the station of leadership in religion, and that they be an exemplar for the righteous in their words and deeds, followed in their actions, trusted in their statements, and the people of goodness walk behind them, guiding and being guided. It is well known that supplicating for the attainment of something is supplicating for what cannot be achieved without it, and this station, the station of leadership in religion, is not achieved except through patience and certainty, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We made them leaders guiding by Our command when they were patient and were certain of Our signs﴾. This supplication therefore entails works, patience in obedience to Allah, patience in refraining from His disobedience, patience in His painful decrees, and complete knowledge which brings its possessor to the station of certainty, along with abundant good and great bounty, and that they be at the highest attainable rank of creation after the messengers.

{75–76} Because their aspirations and their aims are lofty, the recompense was of the same kind as their deeds, so He rewarded them with the lofty dwellings. He said: ﴿Those will be rewarded with the high chambers for what they patiently endured﴾, that is, lofty residences and elegant dwellings encompassing everything desired and pleasing to the eye. They attained what they attained because of their patience, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The angels will enter upon them from every gate, [saying], "Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured. And excellent is the final home."﴾ For this reason He said here: ﴿and they will be met therein with greeting and peace﴾, from their Lord, from His noble angels, and from one another, and they will be safe from all troubles and disturbances.

In sum, Allah described them with gravity, tranquility, and humility toward Him and toward His servants; good manners; forbearance; breadth of character; pardoning the ignorant; turning away from them; repaying their evil with good; standing in prayer at night with sincerity in it; fear of the Fire; supplicating humbly to their Lord that He save them from it; giving what is obligatory and recommended in expenditures; and moderation in that. If they are moderate in spending, in which custom usually leads to neglect or excess, then their moderation and balance in other matters is all the more so. They are also described by safety from major sins; sincerity to Allah in worship; chastity regarding blood and honor; repentance when any of that occurs; not attending gatherings of wrongdoing and immorality, whether in speech or action, and not committing them themselves; keeping themselves far from vain talk and base actions which contain no good. This entails their manliness, their humanity, their perfection, and the elevation of their souls above every base speech and deed. They also meet the signs of Allah with acceptance, understanding of their meanings, acting upon them, and striving to implement their rulings. They supplicate to Allah, the Exalted, with the most complete supplication, in what benefits them and those connected to them, and what benefits the Muslims through the righteousness of their spouses and offspring. A necessary consequence of this is their striving to teach, admonish, and advise them, for whoever desires something and supplicates Allah for it must necessarily be a means toward it. They also asked Allah to attain the highest ranks possible for them, namely the station of leadership and truthfulness. How exalted are these attributes, how lofty these aspirations, how noble these aims, how pure these souls, how clean these hearts, how pure these elite, and how pious these masters! To Allah belongs the favor, blessing, and mercy that enveloped them, and the kindness that brought them to these stations.

It is also a favor of Allah upon His servants that He explained to them their attributes, described to them their conditions, made clear to them their aspirations, and showed them their rewards, so that they would long to be characterized by these attributes, exert their utmost effort toward that, and ask of the One who bestowed favor upon them and honored them, whose bounty is in every time and place and every hour and moment, to guide them as He guided them and to take them under His special care as He took them under His care.

O Allah, to You belongs all praise, to You is the complaint, You are the one sought for help, and to You is the appeal, and there is no power nor strength except with You. We possess for ourselves no benefit nor harm, and we have no ability to attain even an atom's weight of good unless You facilitate it for us. Indeed we are weak and incapable in every respect. We bear witness that if You leave us to ourselves for the blink of an eye, You leave us to weakness, incapacity, and sin. So we trust, O our Lord, only in Your mercy, by which You created us, provided for us, and bestowed upon us Your favors, both apparent and hidden, and turned away from us calamities. So have mercy upon us with a mercy that makes us independent of the mercy of anyone other than You. He who asks You and hopes in You is never disappointed.

{77} Since Allah the Exalted had attributed these servants to His mercy and singled them out for His servitude because of their nobility and excellence, someone might imagine that others too should be included, so why are they not included in servitude? Thus Allah the Exalted informed that He does not care for nor regard anyone other than these, and that were it not for your calling upon Him, the calling of worship and the calling of request, He would not regard you nor love you. So He said: ﴿Say: "My Lord would not concern Himself with you were it not for your supplication. But you have denied, so the penalty will be inevitable."﴾ That is: a punishment that will cling to you as a creditor clings to his debtor, and Allah will judge between you and His believing servants.

The commentary of Surah al-Furqan is complete. So to Allah belongs all praise, thanks, and gratitude, always.
