All of creation shares in this, whether believer or disbeliever, righteous or wicked, for they are all servants of Allah, nurtured and governed by Him. ﴿There is none in the heavens and the earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant﴾.

The second is servitude to His divinity (uluhiyyah), His worship, and His mercy. This is the servitude of His prophets and His friends (awliya'), and it is what is meant here. For this reason He attributed it to His name "the Most Merciful," to indicate that they reached this state only through His mercy. He then mentioned that their attributes are the most perfect attributes and their qualities the most excellent. He described them as ﴿those who walk upon the earth in humility﴾, meaning: calm and humble before Allah and before creation. This is a description of them as possessing gravity, tranquility, and humility before Allah and His servants. ﴿And when the ignorant address them﴾, meaning with the speech of ignorance, as indicated by the attribution of the verb to this description, ﴿they say, "Peace."﴾ That is, they address them with words by which they are safe from sin and safe from responding to ignorance with ignorance. This is praise of them for great forbearance, for repaying evil with good, for pardoning the ignorant, and for the soundness of intellect that brought them to this state.

{64} ﴿And those who spend the night before their Lord, prostrating and standing﴾, meaning: they devote themselves much to the night prayer, sincere in it toward their Lord and humbled before Him, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds, calling upon their Lord in fear and hope, and from what We have provided them they spend. No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes, as reward for what they used to do﴾.

{65} ﴿And those who say, "Our Lord, avert from us the punishment of Hell﴾, meaning: repel it from us by protecting us from its causes and forgiving what has occurred from us that would warrant punishment. ﴿Indeed, its punishment is ever adhering﴾, meaning: it clings to its people as a creditor clings to his debtor.

{66} ﴿Indeed, it is evil as a place of settlement and residence.﴾ This is said by them in humble supplication to their Lord, and to show their great need for Him, and that they have no capacity to bear this punishment. They also remember Allah's favor upon them, for the removal of a hardship is greater in its effect the more severe and dreadful the hardship, and joy in its removal is greater.

{67} ﴿And those who, when they spend﴾, meaning obligatory and recommended expenditures, ﴿neither waste nor are stingy﴾. Waste means exceeding the limit and falling into the category of extravagance. Stinginess means falling into miserliness and avarice, and neglecting obligatory rights. ﴿And their spending is between that﴾, meaning between extravagance and niggardliness, ﴿a means.﴾ They give in obligatory matters, such as zakat, expiations, and obligatory maintenance, and in what is fitting, in the proper manner, without harm or injury. This is from their justice and moderation.

{68} ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity﴾, but worship Him alone, sincere to Him in religion, upright, turning toward Him and turning away from all else. ﴿And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden﴾, meaning the soul of a Muslim and of a disbeliever under covenant, ﴿except by right﴾, such as killing a soul in retaliation, or killing a married adulterer, or a disbeliever whose killing is lawful. ﴿And do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse﴾, but rather guard their private parts, ﴿except with their spouses or what their right hands possess.﴾ ﴿And whoever does that﴾, meaning associating partners with Allah, or killing a soul which Allah has forbidden without right, or fornication, ﴿will meet a penalty.﴾

{69} Then He explained it by His saying: ﴿The punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein humiliated﴾, meaning in the punishment. The threat of eternal abiding applies without doubt to whoever commits all of these, and likewise to whoever associates partners with Allah. Likewise, the threat of severe punishment applies to each of these three, because each is either shirk or among the greatest major sins. As for the eternal abiding of the murderer and the fornicator in punishment, it does not apply to them, because the Qur'anic texts and the prophetic Sunnah have established that all believers will eventually leave the Fire, and no believer will abide in it, no matter what sins he has committed. Allah specified these three because they are the greatest major sins. Shirk entails corruption of religions, killing entails corruption of bodies, and fornication entails corruption of honor.

{70} ﴿Except for one who repents﴾ from these sins and others, by giving them up immediately, regretting what he had done of them in the past, and resolving firmly never to return to them, ﴿and believes﴾ in Allah with sound belief that requires abandoning sins and performing acts of obedience, ﴿and does righteous work﴾ of what the Lawgiver has commanded, when he intends by it the countenance of Allah. ﴿For those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good ones﴾, meaning their actions and words which had been prone to evil deeds will be transformed into good ones. Thus their shirk is transformed into faith, their disobedience into obedience, and the very evil deeds they committed are transformed, after they repent of each sin, turn back in penitence and obedience, into good deeds, as is apparent in the verse. A report concerning this is the hadith of the man whom Allah called to account for some of his sins, enumerating them to him, and then He replaced each evil deed with a good one. He said: "O Lord! I have sins which I do not see here." And Allah knows best. ﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving﴾ to whoever repents, forgiving great sins, ﴿and Merciful﴾ to His servants, for He called them to repentance after they had opposed Him with great sins, then granted them success in it, then accepted it from them.

{71} ﴿And whoever repents and does righteous work — indeed, he turns to Allah with [sincere] return﴾, meaning he should know that his repentance is in the utmost perfection, because it is a return to the path that leads to Allah, which is the very essence of the servant's happiness and success. Therefore let him be sincere in it, and purify it from the impurities of corrupt motives. The purpose of this is to urge the perfecting of repentance and following it in the best and most excellent manner, so that He may advance toward the one who repents to Him and give him his reward according to its perfection.

{72} ﴿And those who do not witness falsehood﴾, meaning they do not attend falsehood, that is, forbidden speech and deeds. Thus they avoid all gatherings that include forbidden speech or forbidden actions, such as delving into the signs of Allah, vain disputation, backbiting, slander, insult, defamation, mockery, forbidden singing, drinking wine, and spreading out silk and images, and the like. If they do not witness falsehood, it is all the more fitting and more certain that they do not utter it or commit it. The bearing of false witness is included under speaking falsehood, and it enters this verse by way of priority. ﴿And when they pass by ill speech﴾, which is speech with no good in it and no religious or worldly benefit, such as the talk of fools and the like, ﴿they pass by with dignity.﴾ That is, they keep themselves pure and honorable, refraining from delving into such things, and they regard delving into them, even if there is no sin in it, as foolishness and a deficiency of humanity and manliness, so they keep themselves far from it. In His saying ﴿when they pass by ill speech﴾ there is an indication that they do not intend to attend it or to listen to it, but if they chance upon it without intention, they keep themselves honorable by avoiding it.

{73} ﴿And those who, when they are reminded of the verses of their Lord﴾, which He commanded them to listen to and to be guided by, ﴿do not fall upon them deaf and blind﴾, meaning they do not meet them with turning away from them, with deafness to hearing them, or with turning their sight and hearts away from them, as those do who do not believe in them or affirm them. Rather their condition regarding them and upon hearing them is as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The only ones who believe in Our verses are those who, when they are reminded of them, fall down in prostration and exalt the praise of their Lord, and they are not arrogant﴾. They meet them with acceptance, with need for them, with submission and surrender to them. You will find with them listening ears and attentive hearts, so their faith increases through them, their certainty is completed through them, they bring them vigor, and they rejoice in them with delight and gladness.

{74} ﴿And those who say, "Our Lord, grant us from among our spouses and offspring comfort for our eyes﴾, meaning our companions, whether friends, peers, or wives, ﴿and offspring who will be a comfort to our eyes﴾, that is, through them our eyes may be comforted. When we consider their condition and attributes, we recognize from their aspirations and the loftiness of their rank that their eyes will not be comforted until they see their spouses and offspring obedient to their Lord, knowing and acting. This supplication for their spouses and offspring for their righteousness is, at the same time, a supplication for themselves, since its benefit returns to them. For this reason they made it a gift to themselves, saying: ﴿Grant us﴾. Moreover, their supplication returns to benefit all Muslims in general, because the righteousness of those mentioned is a cause for the righteousness of many who are connected to them and benefit from them. ﴿And make us a leader for the righteous﴾, that is: bring us, O our Lord, to this high station, the station of the truthful (siddiqin) and the perfected among the righteous servants of Allah, which is the station of leadership in religion, and that they be an exemplar for the righteous in their words and deeds, followed in their actions, trusted in their statements, and the people of goodness walk behind them, guiding and being guided. It is well known that supplicating for the attainment of something is supplicating for what cannot be achieved without it, and this station, the station of leadership in religion, is not achieved except through patience and certainty, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We made them leaders guiding by Our command when they were patient and were certain of Our signs﴾. This supplication therefore entails works, patience in obedience to Allah, patience in refraining from His disobedience, patience in His painful decrees, and complete knowledge which brings its possessor to the station of certainty, along with abundant good and great bounty, and that they be at the highest attainable rank of creation after the messengers.

{75–76} Because their aspirations and their aims are lofty, the recompense was of the same kind as their deeds, so He rewarded them with the lofty dwellings. He said: ﴿Those will be rewarded with the high chambers for what they patiently endured﴾, that is, lofty residences and elegant dwellings encompassing everything desired and pleasing to the eye. They attained what they attained because of their patience, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The angels will enter upon them from every gate, [saying], "Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured. And excellent is the final home."﴾ For this reason He said here: ﴿and they will be met therein with greeting and peace﴾, from their Lord, from His noble angels, and from one another, and they will be safe from all troubles and disturbances.

In sum, Allah described them with gravity, tranquility, and humility toward Him and toward His servants; good manners; forbearance; breadth of character; pardoning the ignorant; turning away from them; repaying their evil with good; standing in prayer at night with sincerity in it; fear of the Fire; supplicating humbly to their Lord that He save them from it; giving what is obligatory and recommended in expenditures; and moderation in that. If they are moderate in spending, in which custom usually leads to neglect or excess, then their moderation and balance in other matters is all the more so. They are also described by safety from major sins; sincerity to Allah in worship; chastity regarding blood and honor; repentance when any of that occurs; not attending gatherings of wrongdoing and immorality, whether in speech or action, and not committing them themselves; keeping themselves far from vain talk and base actions which contain no good. This entails their manliness, their humanity, their perfection, and the elevation of their souls above every base speech and deed. They also meet the signs of Allah with acceptance, understanding of their meanings, acting upon them, and striving to implement their rulings. They supplicate to Allah, the Exalted, with the most complete supplication, in what benefits them and those connected to them, and what benefits the Muslims through the righteousness of their spouses and offspring. A necessary consequence of this is their striving to teach, admonish, and advise them, for whoever desires something and supplicates Allah for it must necessarily be a means toward it. They also asked Allah to attain the highest ranks possible for them, namely the station of leadership and truthfulness. How exalted are these attributes, how lofty these aspirations, how noble these aims, how pure these souls, how clean these hearts, how pure these elite, and how pious these masters! To Allah belongs the favor, blessing, and mercy that enveloped them, and the kindness that brought them to these stations.

It is also a favor of Allah upon His servants that He explained to them their attributes, described to them their conditions, made clear to them their aspirations, and showed them their rewards, so that they would long to be characterized by these attributes, exert their utmost effort toward that, and ask of the One who bestowed favor upon them and honored them, whose bounty is in every time and place and every hour and moment, to guide them as He guided them and to take them under His special care as He took them under His care.

O Allah, to You belongs all praise, to You is the complaint, You are the one sought for help, and to You is the appeal, and there is no power nor strength except with You. We possess for ourselves no benefit nor harm, and we have no ability to attain even an atom's weight of good unless You facilitate it for us. Indeed we are weak and incapable in every respect. We bear witness that if You leave us to ourselves for the blink of an eye, You leave us to weakness, incapacity, and sin. So have mercy upon us with a mercy that makes us independent of the mercy of anyone other than You. He who asks You and hopes in You is never disappointed.

{77} Since Allah the Exalted had attributed these servants to His mercy and singled them out for His servitude because of their nobility and excellence, someone might imagine that others too should be included, so why are they not included in servitude? But you have denied, so the penalty will be inevitable."﴾ That is: a punishment that will cling to you as a creditor clings to his debtor, and Allah will judge between you and His believing servants.

The commentary of Surah al-Furqan is complete. So to Allah belongs all praise, thanks, and gratitude, always.

{64} ﴿And those who spend the night before their Lord, prostrating and standing﴾, meaning: they devote themselves much to the night prayer, sincere in it toward their Lord and humbled before Him, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds, calling upon their Lord in fear and hope, and from what We have provided them they spend. No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes, as reward for what they used to do﴾.

{65} ﴿And those who say, "Our Lord, avert from us the punishment of Hell﴾, meaning: repel it from us by protecting us from its causes and forgiving what has occurred from us that would warrant punishment. ﴿Indeed, its punishment is ever adhering﴾, meaning: it clings to its people as a creditor clings to his debtor.

{66} ﴿Indeed, it is evil as a place of settlement and residence.﴾ This is said by them in humble supplication to their Lord, and to show their great need for Him, and that they have no capacity to bear this punishment. They also remember Allah's favor upon them, for the removal of a hardship is greater in its effect the more severe and dreadful the hardship, and joy in its removal is greater.

{67} ﴿And those who, when they spend﴾, meaning obligatory and recommended expenditures, ﴿neither waste nor are stingy﴾. Waste means exceeding the limit and falling into the category of extravagance. Stinginess means falling into miserliness and avarice, and neglecting obligatory rights. ﴿And their spending is between that﴾, meaning between extravagance and niggardliness, ﴿a means.﴾ They give in obligatory matters, such as zakat, expiations, and obligatory maintenance, and in what is fitting, in the proper manner, without harm or injury. This is from their justice and moderation.

{68} ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity﴾, but worship Him alone, sincere to Him in religion, upright, turning toward Him and turning away from all else. ﴿And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden﴾, meaning the soul of a Muslim and of a disbeliever under covenant, ﴿except by right﴾, such as killing a soul in retaliation, or killing a married adulterer, or a disbeliever whose killing is lawful. ﴿And do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse﴾, but rather guard their private parts, ﴿except with their spouses or what their right hands possess.﴾ ﴿And whoever does that﴾, meaning associating partners with Allah, or killing a soul which Allah has forbidden without right, or fornication, ﴿will meet a penalty.﴾

{69} Then He explained it by His saying: ﴿The punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein humiliated﴾, meaning in the punishment. The threat of eternal abiding applies without doubt to whoever commits all of these, and likewise to whoever associates partners with Allah. Likewise, the threat of severe punishment applies to each of these three, because each is either shirk or among the greatest major sins. As for the eternal abiding of the murderer and the fornicator in punishment, it does not apply to them, because the Qur'anic texts and the prophetic Sunnah have established that all believers will eventually leave the Fire, and no believer will abide in it, no matter what sins he has committed. Allah specified these three because they are the greatest major sins. Shirk entails corruption of religions, killing entails corruption of bodies, and fornication entails corruption of honor.

{70} ﴿Except for one who repents﴾ from these sins and others, by giving them up immediately, regretting what he had done of them in the past, and resolving firmly never to return to them, ﴿and believes﴾ in Allah with sound belief that requires abandoning sins and performing acts of obedience, ﴿and does righteous work﴾ of what the Lawgiver has commanded, when he intends by it the countenance of Allah. ﴿For those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good ones﴾, meaning their actions and words which had been prone to evil deeds will be transformed into good ones. Thus their shirk is transformed into faith, their disobedience into obedience, and the very evil deeds they committed are transformed, after they repent of each sin, turn back in penitence and obedience, into good deeds, as is apparent in the verse. A report concerning this is the hadith of the man whom Allah called to account for some of his sins, enumerating them to him, and then He replaced each evil deed with a good one. He said: "O Lord! I have sins which I do not see here." And Allah knows best. ﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving﴾ to whoever repents, forgiving great sins, ﴿and Merciful﴾ to His servants, for He called them to repentance after they had opposed Him with great sins, then granted them success in it, then accepted it from them.

{71} ﴿And whoever repents and does righteous work — indeed, he turns to Allah with [sincere] return﴾, meaning he should know that his repentance is in the utmost perfection, because it is a return to the path that leads to Allah, which is the very essence of the servant's happiness and success. Therefore let him be sincere in it, and purify it from the impurities of corrupt motives. The purpose of this is to urge the perfecting of repentance and following it in the best and most excellent manner, so that He may advance toward the one who repents to Him and give him his reward according to its perfection.

{72} ﴿And those who do not witness falsehood﴾, meaning they do not attend falsehood, that is, forbidden speech and deeds. Thus they avoid all gatherings that include forbidden speech or forbidden actions, such as delving into the signs of Allah, vain disputation, backbiting, slander, insult, defamation, mockery, forbidden singing, drinking wine, and spreading out silk and images, and the like. If they do not witness falsehood, it is all the more fitting and more certain that they do not utter it or commit it. The bearing of false witness is included under speaking falsehood, and it enters this verse by way of priority. ﴿And when they pass by ill speech﴾, which is speech with no good in it and no religious or worldly benefit, such as the talk of fools and the like, ﴿they pass by with dignity.﴾ That is, they keep themselves pure and honorable, refraining from delving into such things, and they regard delving into them, even if there is no sin in it, as foolishness and a deficiency of humanity and manliness, so they keep themselves far from it. In His saying ﴿when they pass by ill speech﴾ there is an indication that they do not intend to attend it or to listen to it, but if they chance upon it without intention, they keep themselves honorable by avoiding it.

{73} ﴿And those who, when they are reminded of the verses of their Lord﴾, which He commanded them to listen to and to be guided by, ﴿do not fall upon them deaf and blind﴾, meaning they do not meet them with turning away from them, with deafness to hearing them, or with turning their sight and hearts away from them, as those do who do not believe in them or affirm them. {75–76} Because their aspirations and their aims are lofty, the recompense was of the same kind as their deeds, so He rewarded them with the lofty dwellings. He said: ﴿Those will be rewarded with the high chambers for what they patiently endured﴾, that is, lofty residences and elegant dwellings encompassing everything desired and pleasing to the eye. In sum, Allah described them with gravity, tranquility, and humility toward Him and toward His servants; good manners; forbearance; breadth of character; pardoning the ignorant; turning away from them; repaying their evil with good; standing in prayer at night with sincerity in it; fear of the Fire; supplicating humbly to their Lord that He save them from it; giving what is obligatory and recommended in expenditures; and moderation in that. This entails their manliness, their humanity, their perfection, and the elevation of their souls above every base speech and deed. They also meet the signs of Allah with acceptance, understanding of their meanings, acting upon them, and striving to implement their rulings. They supplicate to Allah, the Exalted, with the most complete supplication, in what benefits them and those connected to them, and what benefits the Muslims through the righteousness of their spouses and offspring. A necessary consequence of this is their striving to teach, admonish, and advise them, for whoever desires something and supplicates Allah for it must necessarily be a means toward it. They also asked Allah to attain the highest ranks possible for them, namely the station of leadership and truthfulness. How exalted are these attributes, how lofty these aspirations, how noble these aims, how pure these souls, how clean these hearts, how pure these elite, and how pious these masters! To Allah belongs the favor, blessing, and mercy that enveloped them, and the kindness that brought them to these stations.

It is also a favor of Allah upon His servants that He explained to them their attributes, described to them their conditions, made clear to them their aspirations, and showed them their rewards, so that they would long to be characterized by these attributes, exert their utmost effort toward that, and ask of the One who bestowed favor upon them and honored them, whose bounty is in every time and place and every hour and moment, to guide them as He guided them and to take them under His special care as He took them under His care.

O Allah, to You belongs all praise, to You is the complaint, You are the one sought for help, and to You is the appeal, and there is no power nor strength except with You. {77} Since Allah the Exalted had attributed these servants to His mercy and singled them out for His servitude because of their nobility and excellence, someone might imagine that others too should be included, so why are they not included in servitude? The commentary of Surah al-Furqan is complete. So to Allah belongs all praise, thanks, and gratitude, always.

{67} ﴿And those who, when they spend﴾, meaning obligatory and recommended expenditures, ﴿neither waste nor are stingy﴾. Waste means exceeding the limit and falling into the category of extravagance. Stinginess means falling into miserliness and avarice, and neglecting obligatory rights. ﴿And their spending is between that﴾, meaning between extravagance and niggardliness, ﴿a means.﴾ They give in obligatory matters, such as zakat, expiations, and obligatory maintenance, and in what is fitting, in the proper manner, without harm or injury. As for the eternal abiding of the murderer and the fornicator in punishment, it does not apply to them, because the Qur'anic texts and the prophetic Sunnah have established that all believers will eventually leave the Fire, and no believer will abide in it, no matter what sins he has committed. {70} ﴿Except for one who repents﴾ from these sins and others, by giving them up immediately, regretting what he had done of them in the past, and resolving firmly never to return to them, ﴿and believes﴾ in Allah with sound belief that requires abandoning sins and performing acts of obedience, ﴿and does righteous work﴾ of what the Lawgiver has commanded, when he intends by it the countenance of Allah. ﴿For those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good ones﴾, meaning their actions and words which had been prone to evil deeds will be transformed into good ones. Thus their shirk is transformed into faith, their disobedience into obedience, and the very evil deeds they committed are transformed, after they repent of each sin, turn back in penitence and obedience, into good deeds, as is apparent in the verse. A report concerning this is the hadith of the man whom Allah called to account for some of his sins, enumerating them to him, and then He replaced each evil deed with a good one. He said: "O Lord! I have sins which I do not see here." Therefore let him be sincere in it, and purify it from the impurities of corrupt motives. The purpose of this is to urge the perfecting of repentance and following it in the best and most excellent manner, so that He may advance toward the one who repents to Him and give him his reward according to its perfection.

The bearing of false witness is included under speaking falsehood, and it enters this verse by way of priority. ﴿And when they pass by ill speech﴾, which is speech with no good in it and no religious or worldly benefit, such as the talk of fools and the like, ﴿they pass by with dignity.﴾ That is, they keep themselves pure and honorable, refraining from delving into such things, and they regard delving into them, even if there is no sin in it, as foolishness and a deficiency of humanity and manliness, so they keep themselves far from it. In His saying ﴿when they pass by ill speech﴾ there is an indication that they do not intend to attend it or to listen to it, but if they chance upon it without intention, they keep themselves honorable by avoiding it.

A report concerning this is the hadith of the man whom Allah called to account for some of his sins, enumerating them to him, and then He replaced each evil deed with a good one. He said: "O Lord! I have sins which I do not see here." Therefore let him be sincere in it, and purify it from the impurities of corrupt motives. The purpose of this is to urge the perfecting of repentance and following it in the best and most excellent manner, so that He may advance toward the one who repents to Him and give him his reward according to its perfection.

In His saying ﴿when they pass by ill speech﴾ there is an indication that they do not intend to attend it or to listen to it, but if they chance upon it without intention, they keep themselves honorable by avoiding it.

A report concerning this is the hadith of the man whom Allah called to account for some of his sins, enumerating them to him, and then He replaced each evil deed with a good one. He said: "O Lord! I have sins which I do not see here." And Allah knows best. ﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving﴾ to whoever repents, forgiving great sins, ﴿and Merciful﴾ to His servants, for He called them to repentance after they had opposed Him with great sins, then granted them success in it, then accepted it from them.

{71} ﴿And whoever repents and does righteous work — indeed, he turns to Allah with [sincere] return﴾, meaning he should know that his repentance is in the utmost perfection, because it is a return to the path that leads to Allah, which is the very essence of the servant's happiness and success. Therefore let him be sincere in it, and purify it from the impurities of corrupt motives. The purpose of this is to urge the perfecting of repentance and following it in the best and most excellent manner, so that He may advance toward the one who repents to Him and give him his reward according to its perfection.

{72} ﴿And those who do not witness falsehood﴾, meaning they do not attend falsehood, that is, forbidden speech and deeds. Thus they avoid all gatherings that include forbidden speech or forbidden actions, such as delving into the signs of Allah, vain disputation, backbiting, slander, insult, defamation, mockery, forbidden singing, drinking wine, and spreading out silk and images, and the like. If they do not witness falsehood, it is all the more fitting and more certain that they do not utter it or commit it. The bearing of false witness is included under speaking falsehood, and it enters this verse by way of priority. ﴿And when they pass by ill speech﴾, which is speech with no good in it and no religious or worldly benefit, such as the talk of fools and the like, ﴿they pass by with dignity.﴾ That is, they keep themselves pure and honorable, refraining from delving into such things, and they regard delving into them, even if there is no sin in it, as foolishness and a deficiency of humanity and manliness, so they keep themselves far from it. In His saying ﴿when they pass by ill speech﴾ there is an indication that they do not intend to attend it or to listen to it, but if they chance upon it without intention, they keep themselves honorable by avoiding it.

{73} ﴿And those who, when they are reminded of the verses of their Lord﴾, which He commanded them to listen to and to be guided by, ﴿do not fall upon them deaf and blind﴾, meaning they do not meet them with turning away from them, with deafness to hearing them, or with turning their sight and hearts away from them, as those do who do not believe in them or affirm them. Rather their condition regarding them and upon hearing them is as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The only ones who believe in Our verses are those who, when they are reminded of them, fall down in prostration and exalt the praise of their Lord, and they are not arrogant﴾. They meet them with acceptance, with need for them, with submission and surrender to them. You will find with them listening ears and attentive hearts, so their faith increases through them, their certainty is completed through them, they bring them vigor, and they rejoice in them with delight and gladness.

{74} ﴿And those who say, "Our Lord, grant us from among our spouses and offspring comfort for our eyes﴾, meaning our companions, whether friends, peers, or wives, ﴿and offspring who will be a comfort to our eyes﴾, that is, through them our eyes may be comforted. When we consider their condition and attributes, we recognize from their aspirations and the loftiness of their rank that their eyes will not be comforted until they see their spouses and offspring obedient to their Lord, knowing and acting. This supplication for their spouses and offspring for their righteousness is, at the same time, a supplication for themselves, since its benefit returns to them. For this reason they made it a gift to themselves, saying: ﴿Grant us﴾. Moreover, their supplication returns to benefit all Muslims in general, because the righteousness of those mentioned is a cause for the righteousness of many who are connected to them and benefit from them. ﴿And make us a leader for the righteous﴾, that is: bring us, O our Lord, to this high station, the station of the truthful (siddiqin) and the perfected among the righteous servants of Allah, which is the station of leadership in religion, and that they be an exemplar for the righteous in their words and deeds, followed in their actions, trusted in their statements, and the people of goodness walk behind them, guiding and being guided. It is well known that supplicating for the attainment of something is supplicating for what cannot be achieved without it, and this station, the station of leadership in religion, is not achieved except through patience and certainty, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We made them leaders guiding by Our command when they were patient and were certain of Our signs﴾. This supplication therefore entails works, patience in obedience to Allah, patience in refraining from His disobedience, patience in His painful decrees, and complete knowledge which brings its possessor to the station of certainty, along with abundant good and great bounty, and that they be at the highest attainable rank of creation after the messengers.

{75–76} Because their aspirations and their aims are lofty, the recompense was of the same kind as their deeds, so He rewarded them with the lofty dwellings. He said: ﴿Those will be rewarded with the high chambers for what they patiently endured﴾, that is, lofty residences and elegant dwellings encompassing everything desired and pleasing to the eye. They attained what they attained because of their patience, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The angels will enter upon them from every gate, [saying], "Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured. And excellent is the final home."﴾ For this reason He said here: ﴿and they will be met therein with greeting and peace﴾, from their Lord, from His noble angels, and from one another, and they will be safe from all troubles and disturbances.

In sum, Allah described them with gravity, tranquility, and humility toward Him and toward His servants; good manners; forbearance; breadth of character; pardoning the ignorant; turning away from them; repaying their evil with good; standing in prayer at night with sincerity in it; fear of the Fire; supplicating humbly to their Lord that He save them from it; giving what is obligatory and recommended in expenditures; and moderation in that. If they are moderate in spending, in which custom usually leads to neglect or excess, then their moderation and balance in other matters is all the more so. They are also described by safety from major sins; sincerity to Allah in worship; chastity regarding blood and honor; repentance when any of that occurs; not attending gatherings of wrongdoing and immorality, whether in speech or action, and not committing them themselves; keeping themselves far from vain talk and base actions which contain no good. This entails their manliness, their humanity, their perfection, and the elevation of their souls above every base speech and deed. They also meet the signs of Allah with acceptance, understanding of their meanings, acting upon them, and striving to implement their rulings. They supplicate to Allah, the Exalted, with the most complete supplication, in what benefits them and those connected to them, and what benefits the Muslims through the righteousness of their spouses and offspring. A necessary consequence of this is their striving to teach, admonish, and advise them, for whoever desires something and supplicates Allah for it must necessarily be a means toward it. They also asked Allah to attain the highest ranks possible for them, namely the station of leadership and truthfulness. How exalted are these attributes, how lofty these aspirations, how noble these aims, how pure these souls, how clean these hearts, how pure these elite, and how pious these masters! To Allah belongs the favor, blessing, and mercy that enveloped them, and the kindness that brought them to these stations.

It is also a favor of Allah upon His servants that He explained to them their attributes, described to them their conditions, made clear to them their aspirations, and showed them their rewards, so that they would long to be characterized by these attributes, exert their utmost effort toward that, and ask of the One who bestowed favor upon them and honored them, whose bounty is in every time and place and every hour and moment, to guide them as He guided them and to take them under His special care as He took them under His care.

O Allah, to You belongs all praise, to You is the complaint, You are the one sought for help, and to You is the appeal, and there is no power nor strength except with You. We possess for ourselves no benefit nor harm, and we have no ability to attain even an atom's weight of good unless You facilitate it for us. Indeed we are weak and incapable in every respect. We bear witness that if You leave us to ourselves for the blink of an eye, You leave us to weakness, incapacity, and sin. So we trust, O our Lord, only in Your mercy, by which You created us, provided for us, and bestowed upon us Your favors, both apparent and hidden, and turned away from us calamities. So have mercy upon us with a mercy that makes us independent of the mercy of anyone other than You. He who asks You and hopes in You is never disappointed.

{77} Since Allah the Exalted had attributed these servants to His mercy and singled them out for His servitude because of their nobility and excellence, someone might imagine that others too should be included, so why are they not included in servitude? Thus Allah the Exalted informed that He does not care for nor regard anyone other than these, and that were it not for your calling upon Him, the calling of worship and the calling of request, He would not regard you nor love you. So He said: ﴿Say: "My Lord would not concern Himself with you were it not for your supplication. But you have denied, so the penalty will be inevitable."﴾ That is: a punishment that will cling to you as a creditor clings to his debtor, and Allah will judge between you and His believing servants.

The commentary of Surah al-Furqan is complete. So to Allah belongs all praise, thanks, and gratitude, always.
